tagline: AI-generated slide decks, docs, and one-page sites.
verdictSummary: An outline-to-slides pipeline — ask an LLM for structure, render it into a themed deck, export to PDF — is a real weekend build on top of an open-source slide tool. What's missing is Gamma's polished editing model, its responsive card layouts, and hosted share links with analytics.
coreLoopDIY: Ask an LLM for a slide outline, turn the result into structured slide content, and render it through a themed template into a deck you can preview and export.
whatYouLose: the breadth of their template library
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay because the output looks acceptable immediately, without wrestling with slide software — the generation step is the easy part, the layout and export polish is not.
notes: A strong modern 'kinda': a genuinely viral category with solid open-source and API building blocks already available.
prompt:
Build a command-line slide-deck generator on top of an open-source presentation tool (Slidev is a good fit, since it renders Markdown to slides). Given a topic, call an LLM API for an outline, then generate per-slide content as structured data (title, bullets, speaker notes, a layout name chosen from a small fixed set — title slide, bullet list, two-column, big quote, image-and-text). Render that structured content into the tool's slide format, and support both a live preview and export to PDF. Keep a single theme file for fonts and colors so decks stay visually consistent without redesigning each one. Support regenerating a single slide by number without touching the rest of the deck. Keep decks as plain files on disk, not a database, so they're easy to hand-edit after generation and to keep in version control. If an image-generation API key is present, offer generated images per slide; if it's absent, skip images cleanly rather than failing.

Do not build a web-based visual editor, shareable links with analytics, or real-time collaboration — editing the generated slide file directly is the editor here, and that's the trade for not paying for the hosted product.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Gamma decks?
faq.a: Not directly — Gamma exports to PDF and PPTX, which are fine for viewing but not for re-editing here. Bringing a deck in means re-outlining it as input to the generator, not a structural import.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: Viewing an exported PDF, yes. Generating or editing a deck is a command-line and text-editor workflow, which isn't realistically a phone task.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: LLM API usage per deck, typically a few cents to generate an outline and slide content; hosting isn't needed if you only ever export to PDF locally.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: The responsive card layout Gamma actually renders — text and images that auto-resize to keep a slide balanced regardless of content length. This build uses a small fixed set of layouts, not that adaptive engine.
